units: <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 25b:3">R. Hash. 25ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 17:9">Deut. XVII, 9</cite>) <he>הא אין לך לילך אלא אצל ש׳ שבימיו</he> this teaches that you have to go to him who is the authority in his days (independently of what your opinion about him may be); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 911">Yalk. Deut. 911</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 114:1">Yalk. Sam. 114</cite>.
Ḥag. 14ᵃ (ref. to Is. III, 2) ש׳ זה דיין וכ׳ by shofeṭ is meant the judge that decides a true case according to truth; a. fr.—Pl. שׁוֹפְטִים.

<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 144:3">Sifré Deut. 144</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 16:18">Deut. XVI, 18</cite>) <he>אם יש שוטרים יש ש׳ וכ׳</he> where there are officers (to execute the law), there are judges; where there are no executors, there are no judges. Tanḥ. Shof’ṭim 2, v. <cite ref="U00390"><he>שׁוֹטֵר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 1:2:36">Y. Snh. I, 19ᵃ</cite> bot. (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 21:2">Deut. XXI, 2</cite>) <he>זקניך שהן שׁוֹפְטֶיךָ</he> thy elders that are thy judges.

<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah, Petichta 1">Ruth R. to I, 1</cite> <he>שׁוֹפְטֵיהֶם</he>; <cite ref="Bava Batra 15b:10">B. Bath. 15ᵇ</cite> <he>שׁוֹפְטָיו</he>, v. <cite ref="U01730"><he>שָׁפַט</he></cite>; a. fr.
